text:
marisa: Quick flag — marketing wants to run a global Q4 campaign (Nov 15 - Dec 15). They expect a 2.5-3x jump in embeddings for semantic search and a 1.8x increase in rerank traffic. We need a proposal for capacity + cost tradeoffs by EOD tomorrow.

oliver: Do we have a clean baseline for peak 95th embedding QPS and rerank concurrent queries? I can pull from console but need a starting point.

marisa: Baseline (last 30d peak): embeddings p95 ~11k QPS, rerank concurrent ~420 QPS. Current pools: realtime-embed (A100s, 40 GPUs), realtime-rerank (A100s, 16 GPUs), nightly-batch pool (mixed T4/A10s, 12 GPUs).

samir: Quick napkin calc: if peak goes 3x -> embeddings p95 ~33k QPS. Our embeddings model throughput per A100 GPU at target latency is ~900 QPS (p95), so naive needed GPUs = 33k / 900 = ~37 A100s for realtime just for peak. We're already at 40 though that's for current peak 11k — wait checking numbers.

oliver: Reconcile: current 40 GPUs supporting 11k QPS implies ~275 QPS/GPU observed (because we reserve for latency/SLO and batching behavior). Our production config is conservative because of tail latency. If we tune batching aggressive we can raise to ~700 QPS/GPU but latency p95 goes up ~30-40ms.

marisa: For rerank: model is heavier, throughput ~60 QPS/GPU on A100 at p95. 1.8x of 420 -> 756 concurrent -> needs ~13 GPUs. We currently have 16. So rerank looks okay but headroom might be tight if regional imbalance occurs.

samir: Region constraints: we must support EU and US with <50ms added network. Marketing will target EU + NA. Cant just throw all GPUs in us-west. We need at least a 60/40 split (NA/EU) to avoid cross-region latency. That means for embeddings peak GPUs split: if we need 40 effective GPUs, allocate ~24 NA / 16 EU.

infra-bot: FYI — reserved capacity availability for A100s in eu-west-1 shows limited slots during Nov-Dec; procurement lead time ~3 weeks for dedicated nodes.

taylor: Cost note: A100 spot/discount cost ~ $6.5/hr reserved enterprise rate; A10/T4 cheaper but slower. If we add 24 A100s for 30 days (campaign window) that's 24 * 24 * 30 * $6.5 =~ $112k for NA side alone. Ouch.

marisa: Options to present: 1) Short-term reserved burst pool with autoscale and cross-region fallback (fast but expensive). 2) Hybrid: move embeddings to mixed-precision quantized variant on cheaper GPUs (A10/T4) for batch surge while keeping critical realtime on A100. 3) Defer rerank to lower-cost instances during non-business hours and let async rerank backlog absorb tail.

oliver: Practical plan I propose: - Keep realtime-reank on current 16 A100s + 2 spare for failover. - For realtime-embed create a transient burst pool: 16 A100s in NA + 10 A100s in EU for the peak 4 hours daily (expected highest QPS after campaign emails). - Backfill with quantized A10s for less latency-sensitive windows. - Run canary for 48h before campaign to validate batching settings.

samir: Canary checklist (short):
```
- Deploy quantized model variant to test pool
- Run synthetic replay at 1.5x baseline then ramp to 3x
- Monitor p50/p95 latency, CPU queue, GPU mem pressure
- Validate cross-region failover 99% success under node failure
- Smoke test tracing + costs logging
```

marisa: Also need to estimate GPU-hours and unit cost: can you produce two scenarios (conservative: full A100 scale for whole window; hybrid: burst + quantized backfill)? Put numbers per region.

oliver: I'll run numbers tonight. Quick back-of-envelope for conservative full-A100 scenario for embeddings: assume 40 A100s total * 24h * 30d = 28,800 GPU-hrs. At $6.5/hr = $187,200 for that month just for embeddings baseline capacity. Hybrid burst scenario (burst 4h/day extra 30d): baseline keep 20 A100s steady + burst add 20 A100s for 4h/day -> GPU-hrs = (20*24*30) + (20*4*30) = 14,400 + 4,800 = 19,200 hrs -> $124,800. Swap some baseline to 40 A10s for 24h would be cheaper but throughput hits.

samir: Reminder: networking egress in EU -> US for cross-region fallbacks could add $0.02/GB. If we have 30TB cross-region during surge that's another ~$600. Not huge but worth flagging for ops budget.

taylor: Also watch disk IO for batch backfill nodes — embeddings batch jobs wrote ~8GB/min at peak last year; if we run more batch windows, IOPS limits could throttle and increase job time.

marisa: Great. Deliverables: Oliver — produce two scenario spreadsheets with per-region GPU-hours and cost, and an ops runbook for the burst pool + canary by EOD tomorrow. Samir — short note on network risks and procurement timeline. Taylor — validate disk/IO and confirm which quantized model is safe for rerank fallback. I'll consolidate for leadership.

oliver: On it. Will attach runbook + spreadsheet as comments in this thread when done.

infra-bot: New runbook ticket created: INFRA-3342 (q4-embed-burst-plan).

samir: If anyone wants to sync 1:1 about splitting pool topologies, ping me — we should also consider per-tenant throttles to reduce tail.

marisa: Thanks team. We'll review tomorrow at 10am PT. :thumbsup:
